# Python API

<!-- Generated by validation/make_python_reference.py from crn-craft 0.7.0. Do not edit: run the script with --write. -->

The public names of `crn_craft` 0.7.0: everything in `crn_craft.__all__`, the methods of `Model`, `PreparedEnsemble`, `Result`, `FspResult` and `CompiledLoop`, and `crn_craft.importers`. The page is generated from the signatures and docstrings of the installed package, so it lists what the package does. Examples are in the [guide](../guide/01-install.md); this page has none.

Import the package as `import crn_craft as crn`. `crn_craft.rules` is the API of release 0.6.0 under its old name. It has the same names with the defaults and document versions of 0.6.0; the [migration page](../guide/migrating.md) lists the differences. Code written for it keeps running.

`crn_craft.rules.ensemble` takes the arguments of `ensemble` below. Its `quantiles` defaults to `None` (no quantiles), and an absent `selector` means the linear scan.

Contents: [Models](#models), [Running](#running), [Results](#results), [Files and archives](#files-and-archives), [Analysis and import/export](#analysis-and-importexport), [Compiled loops](#compiled-loops).

## Models

Build a model in Python, or take a packaged one. `Model` writes `crn-craft.model/1.0`. The language of the document is in the [model reference](model-language.md); chapter 2 of the guide teaches the builder.

### `Model`

```text
class Model(name='model')
```

A reaction network over attribute-free species, written as
`crn-craft.model/1.0`.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `'model'` | The model's name. |

The builder of `crn_craft.rules.Model` (the same methods: `add_species`,
`add_parameter`, `add_reaction`, `set_initial`, `set_stop`,
`add_ode`, `to_dict`, `to_json`, `from_dict`, `fsp`,
`analyze`, `to_gillespy2`), whose documents are always
`crn-craft.model/1.0`. `add_reaction` accepts any number of
reactant molecules; `["A", "A", "A"]` is a third-order reaction.

### `Model.add_species`

```text
Model.add_species(name, initial=0)
```

Declare species with initial counts (default 0).

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | required | A species name, or a mapping from names to initial counts. |
| `initial` | `0` | Initial count. Not allowed with a mapping. |

`add_species("S", 999)` declares one; `add_species({"S": 999,
"I": 1})` declares every entry of a mapping, in its order, as one
call each would. A mapping takes no other argument (`TypeError`).
If an entry is invalid, nothing is declared. A species that a
reaction already introduced keeps its position and takes the count.

### `Model.add_parameter`

```text
Model.add_parameter(name, value=<required>)
```

Declare parameters that string rates may read.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | required | A parameter name, or a mapping from names to values. |
| `value` | required | The value. Not allowed with a mapping. |

`add_parameter("gamma", 0.01)` declares one;
`add_parameter({"gamma": 0.01, "beta": 2e-4})` declares every
entry of a mapping, in its order, as one call each would. A mapping
takes no other argument (`TypeError`). If an entry is invalid,
nothing is declared. `add_parameters` is the same method.

### `Model.add_parameters`

```text
Model.add_parameters(name, value=<required>)
```

Declare parameters that string rates may read.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | required | A parameter name, or a mapping from names to values. |
| `value` | required | The value. Not allowed with a mapping. |

`add_parameter("gamma", 0.01)` declares one;
`add_parameter({"gamma": 0.01, "beta": 2e-4})` declares every
entry of a mapping, in its order, as one call each would. A mapping
takes no other argument (`TypeError`). If an entry is invalid,
nothing is declared. `add_parameters` is the same method.

### `Model.add_reaction`

```text
Model.add_reaction(rate, reactants, products, name=None)
```

Add a reaction `reactants -> products`.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rate` | required | A number (a mass-action constant) or a string (the whole propensity). |
| `reactants` | required | Species names, repeated for multiplicity: `["A", "A"]`. |
| `products` | required | Species names, repeated for multiplicity. |
| `name` | `None` | The rule's name. Default `r<index>`. |

`rate` is a number (a mass-action constant k: the reaction fires
at k times the number of distinct combinations of reactant
molecules, so `["A", "A"]` fires at k·A(A−1)/2) or a string (the
whole propensity). Species are lists of names, repeated for
multiplicity, for example `["A", "A"]`. Three or more reactant
molecules, such as `["A", "A", "A"]` or `["A", "A", "B"]`, are
written with the pattern field `count` of `crn-craft.model/1.0`
(a numeric k fires at k·C(A, 2)·B for `["A", "A", "B"]`; a string
propensity applies while each species has its count). Species not
yet declared are declared with count 0, as in rebop. `name`
defaults to `r<index>`.

### `Model.set_initial`

```text
Model.set_initial(counts=None, /, **kwargs)
```

Set initial counts of declared species, from a mapping or keywords.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `counts` | `None` | A mapping from species names to counts. |
| `**kwargs` | none | The same, as keywords: `set_initial(S=990, I=10)`. |

`model.set_initial({"S": 990, "I": 10})` and
`model.set_initial(S=990, I=10)` are equivalent.

### `Model.set_stop`

```text
Model.set_stop(condition)
```

Set the stop condition, or remove it with `None`.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `condition` | required | An expression over parameters and species counts, or `None` to remove the stop. |

`condition` is an expression over parameters and species counts,
for example `"I == 0"` or `"N > 0 && mutants >= 0.9 * N"`. Once
it is true (it is checked at time 0 and after every event), a
replicate keeps its state to the end of the report grid and is
recorded as `"stopped"`, with its `stop_time`. It cannot read
continuous variables; a bound of `add_ode` stops on those.

### `Model.add_ode`

```text
Model.add_ode(
    name,
    initial,
    derivative,
    independent=False,
    lower_bound=None,
    on_bound='stop',
)
```

Declare a continuous variable dx/dt = `derivative` between events.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | required | The variable's name. |
| `initial` | required | A number or a parameter expression. |
| `derivative` | required | An expression over parameters, species counts and continuous variables. |
| `independent` (keyword only) | `False` | `True` if `initial` and `derivative` read only parameters and other independent variables. |
| `lower_bound` (keyword only) | `None` | A number or a parameter expression, or `None`. |
| `on_bound` (keyword only) | `'stop'` | `"stop"` ends the replicate at the bound, `"clamp"` holds the variable there. |

`initial` and `lower_bound` are numbers or parameter expressions;
`derivative` is an expression over parameters, species counts and
continuous variables. String rates may read the variable. With a
`lower_bound`, `on_bound` is `"stop"` (end the replicate when
the variable reaches the bound) or `"clamp"` (hold it there). Run
such a model with `method="hybrid"`.

`independent=True` declares that `initial` and `derivative`
read only parameters and other independent variables, never species
counts, so the ODE can be solved once for the whole run instead of
per replicate. It writes `"independent": true` on the variable and
makes `to_dict` write `crn-craft.rules-model/0.4`; the engine
refuses an independent variable that reads anything else. Without
independent variables the document is rules-model/0.3, as before.
`add_ODE` is the same method.

### `Model.add_ODE`

```text
Model.add_ODE(
    name,
    initial,
    derivative,
    independent=False,
    lower_bound=None,
    on_bound='stop',
)
```

Declare a continuous variable dx/dt = `derivative` between events.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | required | The variable's name. |
| `initial` | required | A number or a parameter expression. |
| `derivative` | required | An expression over parameters, species counts and continuous variables. |
| `independent` (keyword only) | `False` | `True` if `initial` and `derivative` read only parameters and other independent variables. |
| `lower_bound` (keyword only) | `None` | A number or a parameter expression, or `None`. |
| `on_bound` (keyword only) | `'stop'` | `"stop"` ends the replicate at the bound, `"clamp"` holds the variable there. |

`initial` and `lower_bound` are numbers or parameter expressions;
`derivative` is an expression over parameters, species counts and
continuous variables. String rates may read the variable. With a
`lower_bound`, `on_bound` is `"stop"` (end the replicate when
the variable reaches the bound) or `"clamp"` (hold it there). Run
such a model with `method="hybrid"`.

`independent=True` declares that `initial` and `derivative`
read only parameters and other independent variables, never species
counts, so the ODE can be solved once for the whole run instead of
per replicate. It writes `"independent": true` on the variable and
makes `to_dict` write `crn-craft.rules-model/0.4`; the engine
refuses an independent variable that reads anything else. Without
independent variables the document is rules-model/0.3, as before.
`add_ODE` is the same method.

### `Model.add_continuous`

```text
Model.add_continuous(
    name,
    initial,
    derivative,
    lower_bound=None,
    on_bound='stop',
)
```

Deprecated since 0.5.0: use [`add_ode`](#modeladd_ode), which takes the same
arguments and `independent=`. Writes the same document as before.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | required | The variable's name. |
| `initial` | required | A number or a parameter expression. |
| `derivative` | required | An expression over parameters, species counts and continuous variables. |
| `lower_bound` (keyword only) | `None` | A number or a parameter expression, or `None`. |
| `on_bound` (keyword only) | `'stop'` | `"stop"` ends the replicate at the bound, `"clamp"` holds the variable there. |

### `Model.from_dict`

```text
Model.from_dict(document)
```

A model of a complete model document.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `document` | required | A model document: `crn-craft.model/1.0`, a rules-model or a network `model/0.1`. |

`document` is a dictionary, JSON text or bytes: any rules-model
version, `crn-craft.model/1.0` or a network `crn-craft.model/0.1`,
which is converted first ([`crn_craft.convert`](#convert)). The engine
checks it (`CrnError` with its diagnostics if invalid).
[`to_dict`](#modelto_dict) returns the document as given, key order included,
so its hash is that of the document; `crn_craft.Model.from_dict`
writes it as `crn-craft.model/1.0`, changing only the schema
string of a rules-model.

A document the builder could have written (attribute-free types,
one count observable per type named after it, one numeric initial
count per type; rules-model/0.3, 0.4 or model/1.0), which includes
every converted network model and the packaged examples, stays
editable: the `add_*` and `set_*` methods work, and after the
first edit `to_dict` writes the builder's document (explicit
default values such as `"attributes": []` and `"reduce": "sum"`
are then left out, which changes the bytes but not the meaning).
Any other document (attributes, filtered or weighted observables, an
ATP block, ...) is kept whole and cannot be edited: those methods
raise `ValueError`; edit the dictionary and call `from_dict`
again.

### `Model.to_dict`

```text
Model.to_dict()
```

Return the document as a new dictionary.

It is rules-model/0.3, or rules-model/0.4 if a continuous variable
is independent (see [`add_ode`](#modeladd_ode)), or `crn-craft.model/1.0` if
a reaction takes three or more molecules; `crn_craft.Model` writes
`crn-craft.model/1.0` always. A model from [`from_dict`](#modelfrom_dict)
returns its document until it is edited.

### `Model.to_json`

```text
Model.to_json(*, indent=2)
```

Return the document as JSON text with a trailing newline.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `indent` (keyword only) | `2` | JSON indentation. |

### `load_example`

```text
load_example(name)
```

One of the packaged example models as a [`Model`](#model).

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | required | `"enzyme-mechanism"`, `"immigration-death"`, `"michaelis-menten"`, `"repressilator"` or `"vilar-noise"`. |

`name` is one of `"enzyme-mechanism"`,
`"immigration-death"`, `"michaelis-menten"`, `"repressilator"`
and `"vilar-noise"`. The packaged files are the converted
`crn-craft.model/1.0` documents of `models/examples/` in the
repository (`crn_craft.convert` of each); `to_dict()` returns that
document until the model is edited.

## Running

Prepare a request and simulate it, check documents without running them, ask for the finite state projection, and read the discovery document. `ensemble` builds the request from keyword arguments; `prepare` takes a request you wrote. Both return a `PreparedEnsemble`. The guide teaches this in chapters 3 and 5.

### `ensemble`

```text
ensemble(
    model,
    end,
    report_times,
    replicates=1,
    seed=0,
    threads=1,
    keep_paths=0,
    keep_instances=0,
    max_events=1000000,
    max_sampling_steps=8000000,
    max_instances=100000,
    max_output_bytes=67108864,
    wall_time_s=None,
    trackers=(),
    event_log=None,
    method=None,
    compiled=None,
    quantiles=(0.025, 0.5, 0.975),
    selector=None,
)
```

Build and prepare a `crn-craft.run/1.0` request; `simulate()` runs it.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | required | A model: bytes from `load`, a JSON string, a dictionary or a `Model`. |
| `end` (keyword only) | required | Horizon of the run. Report times lie in [0, `end`]. |
| `report_times` (keyword only) | required | Increasing report times in [0, `end`]. |
| `replicates` (keyword only) | `1` | Number of replicates. |
| `seed` (keyword only) | `0` | Root seed. Replicate `i` draws from its own stream, so results do not depend on `threads`. |
| `threads` (keyword only) | `1` | Native worker threads, 1 to 64. |
| `keep_paths` (keyword only) | `0` | How many replicates, from replicate 0, keep their full observable series (`result.paths`). `"all"` or `True` keeps every replicate. |
| `keep_instances` (keyword only) | `0` | How many replicates keep their final instances (`metadata["final_instances"]`). |
| `max_events` (keyword only) | `1000000` | Event budget per replicate. |
| `max_sampling_steps` (keyword only) | `8000000` | Budget per replicate for random words and leap iterations. |
| `max_instances` (keyword only) | `100000` | Most instances alive at once, per replicate. |
| `max_output_bytes` (keyword only) | `67108864` | Budget for the size of the result. Event logs reserve space for every replicate before the run. |
| `wall_time_s` (keyword only) | `None` | Wall-clock limit of the whole run in seconds, or `None`. |
| `trackers` (keyword only) | `()` | A list of `{"observable", "first_passage"?, "keep_episodes"?}`. |
| `event_log` (keyword only) | `None` | `{"max_entries": n, "rules": [...]}`, or `None`. |
| `method` (keyword only) | `None` | A method name or a dictionary such as `{"kind": "tau", "epsilon": 0.03}`; `None` runs the tree method. See [methods](methods.md). |
| `compiled` (keyword only) | `None` | A loop from `compile_loop` for this model. Checked at preparation and used by every `simulate()`. |
| `quantiles` (keyword only) | `(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)` | Probabilities for `statistics["quantiles"]` and `statistics["median"]`. `()` or `None` asks for none. |
| `selector` (keyword only) | `None` | The event selector of `static_direct`: `"linear"`, `"composition_rejection"`, `"sorting"`, `"rssa_cr"` or `"auto"`. See [methods](methods.md#selectors). |

The arguments are those of [`crn_craft.rules.ensemble`](#ensemble), with two
differences: the documents are always `crn-craft.model/1.0` (a
rules-model gets that schema string, a network `crn-craft.model/0.1`
is converted) and `crn-craft.run/1.0`, and `quantiles` defaults to
`(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)`, so `result.statistics` has `"median"` and
`"quantiles"`; `quantiles=()` or `None` asks for none.
`selector` chooses the event selector of `method="static_direct"`
(absent means `"auto"`). `method=None` runs the exact tree method;
higher-order reactions (`count`) need `"static_direct"`,
`"next_reaction"`, `"tau"` or `"hybrid"`.

### `prepare`

```text
prepare(model, request, *, compiled=None, quantiles=<unset>, selector=None)
```

Prepare a request you wrote, as `crn-craft.run/1.0`.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | required | A model: bytes from `load`, a JSON string, a dictionary or a `Model`. |
| `request` | required | A request you wrote: bytes, a JSON string or a dictionary. |
| `compiled` (keyword only) | `None` | A loop from `compile_loop` for this model. Checked at preparation and used by every `simulate()`. |
| `quantiles` (keyword only) | unset | Unset: `(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)` unless the request states `outputs.quantiles` itself. `()` asks for none. |
| `selector` (keyword only) | `None` | The event selector of `static_direct`: `"linear"`, `"composition_rejection"`, `"sorting"`, `"rssa_cr"` or `"auto"`. See [methods](methods.md#selectors). |

As [`crn_craft.rules.prepare`](#prepare), but the documents are always the
1.0 contracts: a rules-run request is rewritten as `crn-craft.run/1.0`
with the defaults of its version written out (so it runs the same
paths), a rules-model gets the schema `crn-craft.model/1.0` and a
network `crn-craft.model/0.1` is converted; the request's model hash
follows when it was the hash of the supplied model. `quantiles`
defaults to `(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)` unless the request states
`outputs.quantiles` itself; `quantiles=()` asks for none. A
`crn-craft.run/1.0` request for `crn-craft.model/1.0` bytes that
needs no change keeps its exact bytes.

### `PreparedEnsemble`

```text
class PreparedEnsemble
```

Created by the functions of this page, not by calling it.

A prepared request, returned by `ensemble` and `prepare`.

`simulate()` runs it, `bind_parameters` makes a candidate with other
parameter values, and `archive` seals a run. It can be simulated again
with independent execution state.

### `PreparedEnsemble.simulate`

```text
PreparedEnsemble.simulate(
    cancel_file=None,
    callback=None,
    batch_callback=None,
    batch_size=256,
    compiled=None,
)
```

Run native workers.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cancel_file` (keyword only) | `None` | Path of a file; the run is cancelled when the file exists. |
| `callback` (keyword only) | `None` | `callback(id, event)` on the native workers; returning `False` stops that replicate. Needs the interpreter. |
| `batch_callback` (keyword only) | `None` | `batch_callback(id, events)` receives the retained log after the run. |
| `batch_size` (keyword only) | `256` | Entries per call of `batch_callback`. |
| `compiled` (keyword only) | `None` | A `CompiledLoop` for this call only. `None` uses the loop attached at preparation, if any. |

A live callback(id, event) returning False stops that replicate; any
other return value continues. `event` is a log entry: `time`,
`rule` (an index into `rule_names`, None for a leap),
`reactants`, `products`, `observables` (in the result's column
order) and `firings`. Workers preserve per-replicate order, and
calls from different replicates interleave. An exception in the
callback cancels the run and is raised here; partial results are
discarded. A callback that blocks also blocks Ctrl-C. A
batch_callback(id, events) replays the retained log after execution
and cannot affect the run.

`compiled`, a [`CompiledLoop`](#compiledloop) for this model, runs this
call in the compiled program instead of the interpreter, with
byte-identical results. The request must select `static_direct`
(`CrnError` `CRN-R020` at `/method` otherwise) and use this
loop's model bytes (`CRN-R020` at `/model`); the first call
checks this. `None`, the default, means the loop attached with
`compiled=` on `ensemble` or `prepare`, and the interpreter
if none was attached. So a run prepared without a loop can be
simulated either way, call by call, while a run with an attached
loop always runs compiled. Callbacks need the interpreter and are
refused with `ValueError` whenever a loop runs the call.

### `PreparedEnsemble.bind_parameters`

```text
PreparedEnsemble.bind_parameters(overrides)
```

Prepare an independent candidate with the same ensemble settings.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `overrides` | required | A mapping from parameter names to new finite values. |

The candidate's model and run hashes cover the re-serialized bound
model and request, not the original file. It runs interpreted: a
compiled loop serves only the model bytes it was compiled for.

Its results' `model` is this run's model with the bound values,
and their `request` this run's request bound to it (see
`Result.model`).

### `PreparedEnsemble.rule_names`

```text
PreparedEnsemble.rule_names
```

Read-only property.

Rule names in declaration order.

Callback events and log entries carry a rule index into this tuple,
so `run.rule_names[event["rule"]]` names the rule that fired.

### `Model.fsp`

```text
Model.fsp(end, report_times, bounds, *, max_states=None, tolerance=None)
```

The exact distribution of the counts by finite state projection.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `end` | required | Horizon of the run. Report times lie in [0, `end`]. |
| `report_times` | required | Increasing report times in [0, `end`]. |
| `bounds` | required | A mapping from every species label to its largest count. |
| `max_states` (keyword only) | `None` | Cap on the enumerated states. `None` means 100,000. |
| `tolerance` (keyword only) | `None` | Truncation budget of the series. `None` means `1e-12`. |

`bounds` maps every species label to its largest count (a type
name for a type without attributes, for example `{"S": 999, "I":
1000, "R": 1000}`); `end` and `report_times` are as in
`ensemble`. `max_states` (default 100,000) caps the enumerated
states and `tolerance` (default `1e-12`) is the truncation
budget of the series. The model must be closed (`CrnError`
`CRN-R017` otherwise). Returns an [`FspResult`](#fspresult); see
`crn_craft.rules.fsp` for the method and its error terms.

### `check`

```text
check(model, request=None)
```

Check a model, and optionally a request for it, without running anything.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | required | A model: bytes, text, a dictionary or a `Model`. |
| `request` | `None` | A request for the model, or `None` to check the model alone. |

`model` and `request` are bytes, text, dictionaries or a
[`Model`](#model). Returns the report `crn-craft check MODEL [REQUEST]`
prints, as a dictionary; read `valid` and `diagnostics`:

- a `crn-craft.model/1.0` model, with or without a request, and a
  rules-model with a request: `crn-craft.check/1.0`; with a request,
  the report says whether `run` would accept the two documents
  (simulation and `fsp` requests) and adds `run_sha256`;
- a rules-model alone: `crn-craft.rules-check/0.1`, as release 0.6.0;
- a network `crn-craft.model/0.1` alone: `crn-craft.check/1.0` of
  the conversion (`CRN-R016` and validation diagnostics if it cannot
  be converted).

### `describe`

```text
describe(kind=None)
```

The discovery document, or the JSON Schema of one contract.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `None` | A contract name such as `"model-1.0"` or `"run-1.0"`. `None` returns the discovery document. |

Without `kind`: `crn-craft.describe/1.0`, as `crn-craft describe`
prints it, with the commands, the 1.0 contracts, methods, selectors,
quantiles and limits first and the older contracts that are still read
under `legacy`. With `kind` (for example `"model-1.0"` or
`"run-1.0"`), the schema `crn-craft describe KIND` prints;
`ValueError` for an unknown kind.

### `CrnError`

```text
class CrnError(diagnostics)
```

A request the native core rejected.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `diagnostics` | required | The list of diagnostics. |

`diagnostics` is the list of CRN-craft diagnostics (dictionaries with
`code`, `path`, `message` and `hint`). It is a `ValueError`, so
existing `except ValueError` handlers keep working.

## Results

What `simulate()` and `Model.fsp` return. The fields of the result document and the terminations are in the [results reference](results.md). `Result.save` is under [files and archives](#files-and-archives). Chapter 4 of the guide teaches the data frames.

### `Result`

```text
class Result
```

Created by the functions of this page, not by calling it.

The result of a rules ensemble.

- `records`: one row per replicate, indexed by replicate id. Columns
  `started`, `termination` (categorical over the values of `crn_craft.rules.TERMINATIONS`:
  `completed`, `stopped` and the reasons a replicate ended early),
  `stop_time`, `events`, `rng_words`, `peak_instances`,
  `created_instances` and `saved_points`.
- `rule_events`: events per replicate (rows) and rule (columns, in
  declaration order).
- `statistics`: None if withheld, else a dict with `samples` (the
  number of replicates included) and one DataFrame per statistic
  (`mean`, `sample_variance`, `mean_standard_error`), indexed by
  report time with one column per observable. A statistic that was not
  computed is None. A run with `quantiles=` also has `quantiles`, a
  dict from each requested probability to a DataFrame of that shape,
  and, when 0.5 was requested, `median`, the DataFrame of
  `quantiles[0.5]` (see [`ensemble`](#ensemble)).
- `paths`: the kept series as an xarray DataArray with dimensions
  (`replicate`, `time`, `variable`); `paths_frame()` gives the
  DataFrame of release 0.4.0, `to_xarray()` a Dataset.
- `event_columns()`: event logs as a DataArray with dimensions
  (`replicate`, `entry`, `variable`); `event_frame()` gives the
  DataFrame of release 0.4.0.
- `tracker_columns(i)`: a tracker's fields as a DataFrame.
- `metadata`: the full result document; `observations` its trackers
  and logs; `record_diagnostics` replicate errors by id.
- `model` and `request`: the model and request documents that ran,
  and `save(path)`, which writes them with the results to one
  markdown or JSON report.

Observables are in result order: sorted by name, then any continuous
variable such as `ATP`. Use `.to_numpy()` on any frame, column or
array for NumPy arrays.

### `Result.paths`

```text
Result.paths
```

Kept series as a DataArray: replicates x report times x variables.

Dimensions are `("replicate", "time", "variable")`, the order of
`event_columns()`, with the coordinates `replicate` (the kept
replicate ids, int64), `time` (the report times) and `variable`
(the observables in result order: sorted names, then continuous
variables). Values
are float64. `attrs` holds the result's `sampler`, `method`
(the method object of rules-result/0.3 as JSON text, `"null"`
for older results), `root_seed`, `model_sha256` and
`run_sha256`; netCDF can store all of them.

`keep_paths` decides which replicates are kept (`"all"` keeps
every one). A replicate that ended on a budget has values only up
to its last saved report time and NaN after it. For example
`paths.sel(variable="mutants")` is a replicate x time array and
`paths.sel(replicate=3)` one replicate's series. Release 0.5.0
ordered the dimensions `("time", "variable", "replicate")`;
`paths.transpose("time", "variable", "replicate")` gives that
order. `paths_frame()` returns the DataFrame of release 0.4.0.

### `Result.paths_frame`

```text
Result.paths_frame()
```

Kept series as a DataFrame: (replicate, time) rows.

One column per observable, in result order; this is `paths` of
release 0.4.0. A replicate that ended on a budget has rows only up
to its last saved report time.

### `Result.to_xarray`

```text
Result.to_xarray()
```

Return the kept paths as an xarray Dataset.

Dimensions are `replicate` and `time` (the report times), with
one variable per observable; rows a replicate did not save are NaN.
It holds the values of `paths`: `paths.to_dataset("variable")`.
`attrs` holds `sampler`, `model_sha256`, `run_sha256` and
`root_seed`, all of which netCDF can store.

### `Result.tracker_columns`

```text
Result.tracker_columns(index=0)
```

Return a tracker's scalar fields, one row per observed replicate.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | `0` | The index of the tracker in the request's `trackers`. |

Indexed by replicate id. Counts (`appearances`, `extinctions`,
`omitted_episodes`) are unsigned integers; times and values are
floats, NaN where absent (for example `first_passage` of a
replicate that never met the predicate). Replicates that failed
before tracking began carry no observation. Episodes are in
`observations`.

### `Result.event_columns`

```text
Result.event_columns(replicate=None)
```

Return retained event logs as a DataArray.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `replicate` | `None` | A replicate id, or `None` for every log. |

Without a replicate id the dimensions are `("replicate", "entry",
"variable")`: one row per observed replicate (int64 ids), entries
0, 1, ... in event order, and the observables after each event
(result order), NaN past a replicate's last entry. Coordinates over
(`replicate`, `entry`): `time` (float64, NaN as padding),
`rule` (the rule index, -1 for a leap, -2 as padding) and
`rule_name` (the name; NaN for a leap and as padding); over
`replicate`: `length`, the number of logged entries. With a
replicate id the dimensions are `("entry", "variable")`, exactly
`length` entries, with scalar `replicate` and `length`
coordinates. `attrs` is that of `paths`.

A replicate without logged events has `length` 0. Participant
instances and leap firings are in the observation entries.
`event_frame()` returns the DataFrame of release 0.4.0.

### `Result.event_frame`

```text
Result.event_frame(replicate=None)
```

Return retained event logs as a DataFrame (release 0.4.0's form).

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `replicate` | `None` | A replicate id, or `None` for every logged event. |

With a replicate id, that replicate's log, indexed by `entry`;
without one, every logged event, indexed by (`replicate`,
`entry`). Rows are in event order: `time`, `rule` (the rule
index, -1 for a leap), `rule_name` (categorical, missing for a
leap), then one column per observable after the event. Participant
instances and leap firings are in the observation entries.

### `Result.model`

```text
Result.model
```

Read-only property.

The model document that ran, as a new dictionary.

For a run from `ensemble` or `prepare` (also with a compiled
loop) it is the parsed model bytes whose SHA-256 is
`metadata["model_sha256"]`. For a `bind_parameters` candidate
it is the template's model with the bound parameter values, all
parameters as floats in name order: the document the engine
re-serialized and ran, apart from fields that serialization adds
with their default values. None for a Result built directly from
a metadata document and columns.

### `Result.request`

```text
Result.request
```

Read-only property.

The request document that ran, as a new dictionary.

For a `bind_parameters` candidate it is the template's request
bound to the candidate's model: `model.sha256` is
`metadata["model_sha256"]`. None for a Result built directly from
a metadata document and columns.

### `FspResult`

```text
class FspResult
```

Created by the functions of this page, not by calling it.

A finite state projection as pandas and xarray objects.

[`Model.fsp`](#modelfsp) returns it; `crn_craft.rules.fsp` returns the document
it wraps.

- `states`: the projected states, a DataFrame indexed by `state`
  (0 is the initial state) with one int64 column per species label.
- `probabilities`: a DataArray with dimensions `("time", "state")`,
  the probability of each state at each report time (the mass that left
  the bounds is not in it; see `truncation`).
- `mean`: the projected first moment of each species at each report
  time, a DataFrame indexed by `time`: Σ p(x)·x over the retained
  states, not renormalized, so it is the mean of the full process only
  up to the leaked mass.
- `truncation`: the error terms per report time, a DataFrame with the
  columns `physical_leakage_estimate` (mass that left the bounds),
  `series_tail_upper_bound`, `discarded_weight_estimate`,
  `mass_defect` and `roundoff_mass_residual`.
- `species`: the species labels; `metadata`: the
  `crn-craft.fsp-result/1.0` document.

## Files and archives

Read model and report files, write reports, and seal a run in an archive directory that can be verified later. The formats are in the [archive reference](archives.md) and the [contracts](contracts.md).

### `load`

```text
load(path)
```

Read a model file and check it; return its exact bytes.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | required | A model file. |

Every model version is read: `crn-craft.model/1.0`, the rules-model
versions and the network `crn-craft.model/0.1`. An invalid model
raises `CrnError` with the diagnostics of [`check`](#check). Pass the
bytes to [`ensemble`](#ensemble) or [`prepare`](#prepare), or to
[`Model.from_dict`](#modelfrom_dict).

### `load_report`

```text
load_report(path)
```

Read a JSON report written by `Result.save`.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | required | A JSON file written by `Result.save`. |

Returns the parsed `crn-craft.report/1.0` document as a dictionary:
`schema`, `crn_craft_version`, `model` and `request` (the
documents that ran) and `result`. Non-finite numbers in it are the
strings `"nan"`, `"inf"` and `"-inf"`. Raises `ValueError` for
a file that is not strict JSON (including duplicate keys) or whose
`schema` is not `crn-craft.report/1.0`.

### `Result.save`

```text
Result.save(path, *, paths=True)
```

Write the model, the request and the results to one report file.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | required | The file. `.md` or `.markdown` writes markdown, `.json` writes `crn-craft.report/1.0`. |
| `paths` (keyword only) | `True` | `False` leaves the single trajectories out. |

The extension of `path` decides the format: `.md` or
`.markdown` for markdown, `.json` for JSON (schema
`crn-craft.report/1.0`, read back with [`load_report`](#load_report)), in
any case; another extension raises `ValueError`. `paths=False`
leaves the single trajectories out. An existing file is replaced;
the report is written to a temporary file in the same directory and
renamed, so a failed write (`OSError`) leaves no partial file.
Returns `path` as a `pathlib.Path`.

The same result always gives the same bytes: there is no timestamp,
host name or timing. The markdown report lists the model (reactions,
start values, parameters, stop condition, continuous variables),
the simulation settings with the sampler, the package version and
both hashes, and the results: terminations, mean events per rule,
the kept trajectories and the summary statistics (quantiles, when
the result has them, in ascending order). Observables follow the
model's species declaration order when every observable is named
after a species type, then continuous variables; otherwise result
order. Each section's lines are in a fenced `text` block, so a
markdown renderer keeps one line per entry. Numbers are written in
shortest round-trip form, integral values without `.0`.

A report is a readable record of a run; an archive is the sealed,
verifiable record of a run for replay. `save` changes nothing
about the result.

### `archive`

```text
archive(model, request, directory, *, cancel_file=None)
```

Run a request and seal the run in a new archive directory.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | required | A model: bytes from `load`, a JSON string, a dictionary or a `Model`. |
| `request` | required | A request: bytes, a JSON string or a dictionary. |
| `directory` | required | The new archive directory. It must not exist; its parent must. |
| `cancel_file` (keyword only) | `None` | Path of a file; the run is cancelled when the file exists. |

`model` is model bytes, a JSON string, a dictionary or a
[`Model`](#model); `request` is request bytes, a JSON string or a
dictionary: any rules-run version, or `crn-craft.run/1.0` with any
method, `fsp` included. The request must bind the exact model bytes
(`model.sha256`); its `model.path` is kept but not resolved.
`directory` must not exist; its parent must.

The directory gets `model.json` and `request.json` (the exact
bytes), `result.json` (the result as `crn-craft rules` prints it),
`manifest.json` (`crn-craft.archive/1.0`: length and SHA-256 of the
three) and, written last, `COMPLETE`. This is
`crn-craft rules MODEL REQUEST --archive NEW_DIRECTORY` without files
for the inputs; [`PreparedEnsemble.archive`](#preparedensemblearchive) archives a prepared
run.

Returns the `crn-craft.archive-check/1.0` report as a dictionary,
also when the run or the write failed: read `valid` (the archive was
written), `simulation_complete` (the run completed) and
`termination` together, and `diagnostics` for the reason of a
failure. Input errors create no directory. Check an archive later with
[`verify_archive`](#verify_archive). Ctrl-C cancels the run, which is archived as
cancelled before `KeyboardInterrupt` is raised.

An archive is the sealed, verifiable record of a run for replay; a
report written by [`Result.save`](#resultsave) is a readable record.

### `PreparedEnsemble.archive`

```text
PreparedEnsemble.archive(directory, *, cancel_file=None)
```

Run this request once more and seal the run in `directory`.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `directory` | required | The new archive directory. Its parent must exist. |
| `cancel_file` (keyword only) | `None` | Path of a file; the run is cancelled when the file exists. |

As [`archive`](#archive) with the exact model and request bytes this run
was prepared from: the archived result equals the result of
`simulate()` (completed runs replay byte for byte; a compiled loop
gives the interpreter's result, which the archive holds). Returns
the `crn-craft.archive-check/1.0` report. A `bind_parameters`
candidate has no original bytes and raises `ValueError`: archive
its model with the bound values and a request bound to it with
[`archive`](#archive).

### `verify_archive`

```text
verify_archive(directory)
```

Check an archive directory without running anything.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `directory` | required | The archive directory to check. |

Reads `crn-craft.archive/1.0` directories (written by [`archive`](#archive)
and `crn-craft run ... --archive`) and returns the report of
`crn-craft verify DIRECTORY` as a dictionary
(`crn-craft.archive-check/1.0`): `valid` is true for an intact,
consistent archive, also of an incomplete run (`simulation_complete`
false); `diagnostics` names the first inconsistency otherwise. The
network engine's `crn-craft.archive/0.1` directories are no longer
read (release 0.7.0).

## Analysis and import/export

Analyze the structure of a network, export it, and import SBML and BioNetGen files. The reports are described in the [analysis reference](analysis.md) and the [GillesPy2 export](gillespy2-export.md). Chapter 11 of the guide teaches this.

### `Model.analyze`

```text
Model.analyze()
```

The network analysis of this model (`crn-craft.analysis/1.0`).

Returns the report as a dictionary, as `crn-craft analyze MODEL`
prints it: species and reactions of the lowered network, their
dependencies, conservation laws, the cone of reachable directions,
the complex graph and warnings. Read `success` first: a model
without a flat view (continuous variables, ATP, products that
create new attribute tuples) gives `success` false with
`CRN-R017`.

### `Model.to_gillespy2`

```text
Model.to_gillespy2()
```

This model as a `gillespy2.Model`.

GillesPy2 must be installed, in the version the export names
(`crn-craft describe` lists it; another version raises
`RuntimeError`). A rule with a constant `rate` and at most two molecules becomes a
mass-action reaction, any other rule a custom propensity, as
`crn-craft export MODEL gillespy2` writes them. A model the export
refuses raises `CrnError` (`CRN-E050` for what GillesPy2 cannot
evaluate, such as a stop condition or `exp`).

### `convert`

```text
convert(model)
```

Convert a network model (`crn-craft.model/0.1`) into `crn-craft.model/1.0`.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | required | A model: bytes from `load`, a JSON string, a dictionary or a `Model`. |

`model` is bytes, text or a dictionary. Returns the converted model's
exact bytes (pretty-printed JSON with a trailing newline), the same
bytes `crn-craft convert MODEL` prints. Every species becomes a type
and an observable of the same name, every reaction a rule with the same
propensity; reactions of any order use the pattern field `count`. A
model the converter cannot hold (a population limit, a network without
reactions, ...) raises `CrnError` with `CRN-R016`; an invalid
network model raises `CrnError` with its validation diagnostics.
`Model.from_dict(json.loads(convert(m)))` gives a [`Model`](#model).

### `read_sbml`

```text
read_sbml(path, *, convention)
```

Import an SBML file as a [`Model`](#model).

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | required | An SBML file. |
| `convention` (keyword only) | required | Must be `"stochastic_count_propensity"`. |

The SBML subset and the required `convention`
(`"stochastic_count_propensity"`) are those of
[`crn_craft.importers.import_sbml`](#importersimport_sbml). The network is converted to
`crn-craft.model/1.0`; `model.import_report` keeps the import
report's provenance (`source_format`, `source_sha256`, the
convention and parameter policy) without the model. Unsupported input
raises `crn_craft.importers.ImportFailure` (a `ValueError`).

### `read_bngl`

```text
read_bngl(path, *, convention)
```

Import an expanded BioNetGen network (`.net`) as a [`Model`](#model).

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | required | An expanded `.net` file. |
| `convention` (keyword only) | required | `"binomial"` or `"falling_factorial"`. |

`convention` is the rate convention of
[`crn_craft.importers.import_bng_net`](#importersimport_bng_net) (`"binomial"` or
`"falling_factorial"`). The network is converted to
`crn-craft.model/1.0`; `model.import_report` keeps the import
report's provenance (species patterns, groups, the convention) without
the model. Unsupported input raises
`crn_craft.importers.ImportFailure` (a `ValueError`).

### `importers.import_sbml`

```text
importers.import_sbml(raw, *, convention)
```

L3V2 Core, one fixed unit compartment, integer item amounts, polynomial jumps.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `raw` | required | The SBML document's bytes. |
| `convention` (keyword only) | required | Must be `"stochastic_count_propensity"`. |

convention must be explicitly 'stochastic_count_propensity'. Parameters are
folded into reaction coefficients; the report names that import-time choice.
Returns a `crn-craft.import/1.0` report as a dictionary:
`report["model"]` is the converted `crn-craft.model/1.0` model, beside
the source format and its SHA-256. Unsupported input raises
[`crn_craft.importers.ImportFailure`](#importersimportfailure).

### `importers.import_bng_net`

```text
importers.import_bng_net(raw, *, rate_convention)
```

Expanded numeric .net only; explicit binomial or falling_factorial convention.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `raw` | required | The `.net` file's bytes. |
| `rate_convention` (keyword only) | required | `"binomial"` or `"falling_factorial"`. |

Returns a `crn-craft.import/1.0` report as a dictionary:
`report["model"]` is the converted `crn-craft.model/1.0` model, beside
the source format and its SHA-256. Unsupported input raises
[`crn_craft.importers.ImportFailure`](#importersimportfailure).

### `importers.ImportFailure`

```text
class importers.ImportFailure
```

Raised by an importer for input it does not support.

A `ValueError` with the attribute `code` `"CRN-E090"`.

## Compiled loops

Build the Static Direct event loop of a model into a program and run requests with it. This needs a Rust toolchain; the requirements, the cache and the limits are in the [methods reference](methods.md#compiled-event-loops). Chapter 5 of the guide teaches when to use it.

### `compile_loop`

```text
compile_loop(
    model,
    cache_dir=None,
    cargo='cargo',
    source=None,
    progress=True,
)
```

Compile the Static Direct event loop of a model; opt-in, needs Rust.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | required | A model: bytes from `load`, a JSON string, a dictionary or a `Model`. |
| `cache_dir` (keyword only) | `None` | Where to keep builds. Default: the user cache directory, or `CRN_CRAFT_CACHE_DIR`. |
| `cargo` (keyword only) | `'cargo'` | The cargo executable. |
| `source` (keyword only) | `None` | A CRN-craft checkout of the installed version, for an offline build or a version that is not on crates.io. Default: `CRN_CRAFT_SOURCE`. |
| `progress` (keyword only) | `True` | `False` silences cargo's progress on stderr. |

As [`crn_craft.rules.compile_loop`](#compile_loop), for the document that
[`ensemble`](#ensemble) runs: a rules-model gets the schema string
`crn-craft.model/1.0` and a network `crn-craft.model/0.1` is
converted. So `ensemble(model, ..., compiled=compile_loop(model))`
works for the same `model` argument. Generated loops run the linear
scan: pass `selector="linear"` to [`ensemble`](#ensemble) unless `"auto"`
picks it for the model.

### `loop_source`

```text
loop_source(model)
```

Return the generated Static Direct event loop of a model as Rust.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | required | A model: bytes, text, a dictionary or a `Model`. |

As [`crn_craft.rules.loop_source`](#loop_source), for the document that
[`ensemble`](#ensemble) runs: a rules-model gets the schema string
`crn-craft.model/1.0` and a network `crn-craft.model/0.1` is
converted, so the loop's fingerprint is that of the model/1.0 bytes.

### `CompiledLoop`

```text
class CompiledLoop
```

Created by the functions of this page, not by calling it.

A compiled Static Direct event loop for one model and parameter set.

Returned by [`compile_loop`](#compile_loop). Pass it as `compiled=` to
`rules.ensemble`, `rules.prepare` or `PreparedEnsemble.simulate`
to run Static Direct requests for exactly this model with it.

- `fingerprint`: the generated loop's fingerprint, which covers the
  emitted source and the model bytes;
- `model_sha256`: SHA-256 of the model bytes it was compiled for;
- `version`: the `crn-craft` version it was built against;
- `path`: the program; `directory` its cache entry with the Cargo
  project and `log` the build log;
- `cached`: whether a cached build was reused; `build_seconds` the
  cargo time of a new build, else None.

### `CompiledLoop.execute`

```text
CompiledLoop.execute(request, *, cancel_file=None)
```

Run a rules-run request for this loop's model in its program.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `request` | required | A rules-run request for this loop's model. |
| `cancel_file` (keyword only) | `None` | Path of a file; the run is cancelled when the file exists. |

Returns the metadata text and the record columns, as the extension
does. A rejected request raises `CrnError`.

### `CompiledLoop.verify`

```text
CompiledLoop.verify(run)
```

Run a prepared ensemble interpreted and compiled, and compare.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `run` | required | A `PreparedEnsemble` for this loop's model. |

Raises `CompiledLoopError` (reason `"mismatch"`) unless the
metadata and every record column are byte-identical. Returns the
result.

### `CompiledLoopError`

```text
class CompiledLoopError(message, reason, log=None)
```

A compiled event loop could not be built, or it disagreed with the
interpreter.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | required | The message. |
| `reason` | required | `"cargo_missing"`, `"build_failed"` or `"mismatch"`. |
| `log` | `None` | The path of the build log, if a build started. |

`reason` is `"cargo_missing"`, `"build_failed"` or `"mismatch"`;
`log` is the path of the build log, if a build started.

## The importers module

Explicit finite-network import subsets. No silent SBML/rule expansion.

The importers build a network model (`crn-craft.model/0.1`) exactly as in
0.6.0, validate it, and return it converted to `crn-craft.model/1.0` by
[`crn_craft.convert`](#convert), inside a `crn-craft.import/1.0` report that keeps
the source's provenance. `report["model"]` is the converted model as a
dictionary, ready for the unified API (a later `read_sbml`/`read_bngl`
wraps it in a `Model`).
